title: Neck & Cervical Care
summary: Gentle, upright neck glides and shoulder blade support to ease forward-head screen strain.
whatHelps: Keep your head stacked over your shoulders with micro chin nods.
Support your forearms on armrests or the desk to take weight off your neck.
Raise your laptop or monitor so the top third of the screen is at eye level.
pacingRules: Take a 60-second posture break every 30–45 minutes of screen work.
Keep stretches at a 2 or 3 out of 10 sensation — never pull on your head.
modifyOrSkip: Skip full neck circles or rolling your head backward.
Avoid heavy overhead lifting or holding a phone between ear and shoulder.
Skip deep side-neck pulls with your hand.
deskTips: Bring your screen closer instead of leaning your chin forward.
Check if you are clenching your jaw — let your tongue rest softly.
redFlags: Numbness, tingling, or pins-and-needles radiating down your arm or fingers.
Sudden weakness in your grip or arm.
Dizziness, visual changes, or severe headache with neck movement.

title: Upper Back & Rounded Shoulders
summary: Open tight chest muscles and gently wake up the mid-back muscles that support effortless posture.
whatHelps: Frequent chest openers and slow shoulder rolls.
Gentle seated spinal waves to restore mid-back motion.
Deep rib-expanding breaths to release stiffness between shoulder blades.
pacingRules: Alternate between sitting back against your chair support and sitting tall.
The best posture is your next posture — shift position often.
modifyOrSkip: Avoid forcing your shoulders back rigidly for hours.
deskTips: Keep mouse and keyboard close so your elbows stay near your sides.
Rest your upper back against a supportive chair backrest.
redFlags: Chest pain, pressure, or shortness of breath.
Sharp pain when taking a breath that does not ease with rest.

title: Lower Back Comfort & Support
summary: Decompress sitting load with hip hinges, gentle pelvic tilts, and short walking breaks.
whatHelps: Stand up every 30–45 minutes for even 60 seconds to unload spinal discs.
Use a small rolled towel or cushion behind your lower back when seated.
Move from your hips with soft knees when bending.
pacingRules: On high-stiffness days, choose shorter 1–2 minute standing or walking resets.
Keep all movements smooth and within a pain-free zone.
modifyOrSkip: Skip unsupported toe-touches or deep rounded-back bending.
Avoid loaded spinal twists or sudden jerky movements.
deskTips: Keep both feet flat on the floor (or a footrest) rather than crossing legs for hours.
Hips should be level with or slightly higher than your knees.
redFlags: Shooting pain, numbness, or tingling down the back of your leg.
New weakness in your foot or leg.
Any changes in bladder or bowel control (seek urgent medical care).

title: Shoulder Ease & Mobility
summary: Smooth, below-shoulder-height movement to nourish the joint without pinching.
whatHelps: Pendulum-like easy arm swings and low shoulder rolls.
Setting your shoulder blades gently before reaching.
Supporting your arms on desk pads while typing.
pacingRules: Keep reaches below 90 degrees (shoulder height) if overhead motion feels pinchy.
modifyOrSkip: Skip deep dips, heavy push-ups, or forcing arms overhead against a wall.
deskTips: Bring the mouse closer so you are not reaching forward all day.
redFlags: Inability to lift your arm after a fall or sudden pop.
Pain radiating from chest/left shoulder with shortness of breath.

title: Wrist, Hand & Typing Relief
summary: Neutral-wrist habits and smooth tendon glides for heavy keyboard, laptop, and phone use.
whatHelps: Keep wrists floating straight (neutral) rather than bent upward on the desk edge.
Do 30-second finger and tendon glides between long typing blocks.
Use a light touch on keys and mouse.
pacingRules: Take micro-pauses where you let your hands rest completely open in your lap.
modifyOrSkip: Skip planks, floor push-ups, or bearing body weight on bent wrists.
deskTips: Flatten the back feet of your keyboard so it does not tilt upward into your wrists.
redFlags: Persistent numbness or tingling in your thumb and first three fingers (especially at night).
Dropping objects or noticeable loss of thumb strength.

title: Knee-Friendly Movement
summary: Gentle circulation and quad support with zero jumping, kneeling, or deep knee bends.
whatHelps: Seated knee extensions to gently nourish the joint cartilage.
Using a higher chair and armrests when standing up.
Short, flat-surface walks at an easy pace.
pacingRules: Use a comfortable, shallow range of motion on any standing leg exercise.
modifyOrSkip: Skip deep squats, lunges, jumping, or kneeling on hard floors.
deskTips: Avoid tucking your feet tightly under your chair for long periods; let knees rest at 90–100 degrees.
redFlags: Sudden swelling, redness, or heat around the knee joint.
The knee locking, catching, or giving way when you put weight on it.

title: Hip & Glute Unlocker
summary: Counteract tight hip flexors and sleepy glutes from hours in a chair.
whatHelps: Standing up to open the front of your hips.
Seated figure-four stretch (or ankle cross) with a tall spine.
Short walking breaks to wake up glute circulation.
pacingRules: Alternate sitting and standing if you have an adjustable surface, or stand during phone calls.
modifyOrSkip: Avoid forcing your knee down in hip stretches.
deskTips: Uncross your legs and sit evenly on both sit bones.
redFlags: Sharp groin pain with weight-bearing or radiating leg numbness.

title: Ankle & Foot Circulation
summary: Pump fresh blood flow through your lower legs and keep ankles supple.
whatHelps: Seated ankle pumps and alphabet circles under your desk.
Supporting your feet flat on the floor or a footrest.
Comfortable, supportive footwear during standing or walking.
pacingRules: Prefer seated mobility on days when your feet or ankles feel tender.
modifyOrSkip: Skip hopping, high-impact cardio, or unstable single-leg balances.
deskTips: Do 10 slow ankle pumps every hour to prevent lower-leg heaviness.
redFlags: One-sided calf swelling, warmth, or tenderness (seek prompt medical evaluation).
Inability to bear weight on your foot.

title: Screen Eyes & Headache Care
summary: 20-20-20 visual resets, blinking reminders, and brow/neck relaxation.
whatHelps: Every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Warm palm cupping over closed eyes to relax ocular muscles.
Softening jaw, temple, and neck tension.
pacingRules: Pair every water sip with a 20-second look out the window.
modifyOrSkip: Avoid bright screen glare or tiny font sizes that make you squint and lean forward.
deskTips: Keep your screen an arm's length away and slightly below eye level.
redFlags: Sudden vision changes, flashing lights, or severe headache.

title: Long-Sitting Stiffness Relief
summary: Break up marathon desk blocks with 2-minute whole-body circulation resets.
whatHelps: Standing up for 1–2 minutes every 45 minutes.
Combining a glass of water with a quick shoulder roll and hip stretch.
pacingRules: Consistency beats intensity: four 2-minute resets beat one exhausting workout.
modifyOrSkip: Never jump straight from 4 hours of sitting into fast, heavy movement without a 60-second warm-up.
deskTips: Stand up whenever you take a phone call or wait for a file to load.
redFlags: Sharp joint pain or dizziness when standing up quickly.

title: Calm Energy & Stress Reset
summary: Gentle breath-led movement that wakes up circulation without draining your battery.
whatHelps: Slow nasal breathing with a longer exhale (4s in, 6s out).
Opening the chest and unclenching the shoulders.
Stepping near natural daylight for 2 minutes.
pacingRules: On tired days, 60 seconds of seated breathing + shoulder rolls counts as a full win.
modifyOrSkip: Skip high-intensity workouts when you feel depleted or sleep-deprived.
deskTips: Keep a water glass on your desk — mild dehydration often feels like afternoon fatigue.
redFlags: Dizziness, chest tightness, or persistent exhaustion.
